name: Alex Karp

summary.text: Alex Karp is chief executive and a director of Palantir Technologies, which he co-founded with Peter Thiel and others. SEC Form 4 filings record that he sells Palantir Class A shares under Rule 10b5-1 trading plans, including sales in August 2026 at roughly $172 to $176 per share; press reports put his 2024 sales at about 40.7 million shares for roughly $2 billion. In July 2025 the U.S. Army announced a ten-year enterprise agreement with Palantir capped at $10 billion that consolidated 75 existing contracts. Jacob Helberg, now an Under Secretary of State, previously worked as a senior adviser to Karp.

facts.claim: A Form 4 filed with the SEC for transactions dated August 20, 2026 lists Karp as a director and officer of Palantir and states that the transactions were made under a Rule 10b5-1(c) trading plan; it records a conversion of derivative securities into about 402,348 Class A shares followed by open-market sales at roughly $172 to $176 per share.

sources.title: Palantir Technologies Inc. - Form 4 (Alexander C. Karp)

facts.claim: TipRanks reported in 2025 that Karp adopted a Rule 10b5-1 plan to sell up to 9,975,000 Palantir shares through September 12, 2025, and in doing so canceled a previous plan covering 48.9 million shares worth about $6.01 billion.
facts.quote: In filing the new 10b5-1 trading plan, Karp canceled a previous plan that would have seen him sell much more stock.

sources.title: Palantir (PLTR) CEO Alex Karp to Sell $1.2 Billion of Company Stock

facts.claim: The Motley Fool reported in February 2025 that Karp sold 40.7 million Palantir shares in 2024 at an average price of $47.99, for proceeds of about $2 billion, and that sales on February 20 and 21, 2025 of 194,792 Class A shares were made under a 10b5-1 plan to cover tax obligations on the conversion of Class B stock.
facts.quote: Karp sold 40.7 million shares at an average price of $47.99, for total proceeds of about $2 billion

facts.claim: On July 31, 2025 the U.S. Army announced a ten-year Enterprise Agreement with Palantir capped at $10 billion, replacing 75 separate contracts (15 prime and 60 related) through which it had been buying Palantir products. The Army said the $10 billion figure is the maximum potential value, not a commitment, and that the agreement sets volume-based discounts. The contracting activity was Army Contracting Command, Rock Island Arsenal.
facts.quote: the maximum potential value of the contract, not any specific obligations or commitments
